verdict.rationale: Exa's core interfaces take natural-language input. Search accepts natural-language queries [exa-docs-22, exa-docs-60, exa-docs-36]. Websets start from a natural-language query plus criteria [exa-docs-28, exa-docs-8]. The Answer and Agent APIs return natural-language and structured answers [exa-gh-3, exa-docs-47]. The hosted MCP server and `agent_run` tool let users drive search, research and enrichment by talking to Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT without writing code [exa-docs-40, exa-docs-50, exa-docs-30]. Community hands-on reports show natural-language queries work but with uneven relevance, e.g. about 30/70 hit rate and Websets misses [exa-comm-2, exa-comm-4]. missing for 10: no evidence that account, key or billing management can be done via natural language; independent reports show inconsistent fidelity in interpreting natural-language queries.
